review_summary: Static review of the T330 reporting-policy helper and the schema2 archive integration only. Most of the approved design holds up. Version1 stays on the raw-digest path with an equivalent accept set. Version2 is selected only by explicit approval schema 2 and a fixed sibling sidecar. Update-only rules need exactly one writer actor with an exact Integration/always match. Protection rules need empty actors and only {deletion, non_fast_forward}. Metadata, repository, ID, branch, writer and role are bound. Actors are never invented, since capture requires a visible bypass_actors field. Parser and canonicalization bounds hold for the shapes I traced. Origin, projection-checkpoint and stage rechecks all route through the new digest helper. I traced the sidecar-tamper path and did not find an authority gap. updated_at is part of the approval-bound metadata digest, so a hidden actor edit that moves updated_at fails the digest check whatever the sidecar says. I found one concrete clock defect: the sidecar's future-timestamp check ignores the caller's clock. The verdict is changes_requested only because the output rule is pass-with-no-findings. This does not certify the rest of T287, live activation, App capability or Spec014, and it infers no approval from the self-reported tests.

findings.title: Sidecar future-timestamp check uses the wall clock, not the caller's injected clock
findings.reason: load() has no `now` parameter. Line 153 compares each sidecar observed_at to metadata.clock(None), which is the real current time. Archive _approved_policy_digest accepts `now` and forwards it to validate() (archive line 162), but it cannot forward it to load() (archive line 158). This gives two clock domains within one verification. (1) When the live API still shows bypass_actors, validate() returns 'direct' at line 124 before the observed <= current check at line 129. A sidecar record dated after the caller-supplied `now` is therefore accepted, provided it is not in the wall-clock future. (2) With a caller `now` later than the wall clock, valid records are rejected at line 153. Results depend on the host clock rather than the supplied one, so replay and fixed-clock verification are not deterministic. The test fixture uses a fixed now=2026-10-16 and has no case covering the load() future or settle check, so this is untested. Fix: add a keyword `now=None` to load(), use metadata.clock(now) at line 153, and pass `now` at archive line 158.

limitations: Static review only. Nothing was executed and no test results are claimed.

Only the supplied excerpts of factory-receipt-archive.py were visible. Lines 346-755, 895-914 and 1015-1139 were not shown, including append_delivery and the retained_* and projection_* helpers. I cannot confirm that no other call site still compares the raw digest(canonical(ruleset)) against approval['policies']. Any such site would fail closed under schema2, but it would be a functional break.

Sidecar content is not hash-bound by the approval or by the origin and projection bindings. validate() computes observation_sha256, but _approved_policy_digest drops it. I judged this not to be an authority failure: actors are forced to the exact expected value, and role, metadata digest and updated_at must match live data. It does rely on GitHub changing updated_at on every actor edit. That is an external assumption I could not verify.

In direct mode (the API shows bypass_actors), sidecar records are format-checked only. They are not cross-checked against the live policy, so a stale or mismatched sidecar passes until the API hides actors. This is not an authority failure.

_canonical does not catch RecursionError. Very deep nesting could surface as a non-ValueError exception from json.dumps instead of a clean rejection. The decode path already converts parse-time recursion errors to ValueError. This is a malformed-input denial style and fails closed.

load() does not reject symlinks, FIFOs or other special files at the sidecar path. observe()/main() have no error handling and leave exceptions as tracebacks. The archive module eagerly executes the reporting module at import, so a load failure there would also break version1 flows. These are optional hardening items.

Reporting branch validation is stricter than the archive branch regex, for example in segments ending in '.' or '.lock'. Such approvals fail closed under schema2 with a message about the reporting branch. This is acceptable but may surprise operators.

Whether GitHub returns bare {'type':'update'} for update rules, and whether it bumps updated_at on bypass-actor edits, is external API behavior I could not verify. Nothing was verified about live App capability, installation or permissions.
